column1: # The plan says *which relation* is asserted. This lexicon says *which case the
# head governs*. The linearizer computes the forms. Before this file the
# government lived inside 127 template strings, so `{OBJ|acc}` had to be
# rewritten per template and could disagree with itself.
#   finite    a finite verb; Russian present tense agrees in person and number
#             but not in gender, so one surface serves every subject.
#   agreeing  a short participle or short adjective; it agrees with the subject
#             in gender and number, so four forms are required.
#             `head_forms` is masc,fem,neut,plur in that fixed order.
#   none          the head takes no complement          (время необратимо)
#   prep:P:CASE   preposition plus case                 (зависит от + gen)
#   uninflected   an infinitive phrase or predicate      (может + inf)
# Three legacy relation ids — napravlena, svyazan, neobratimo — encode a
# subject gender in the identifier itself, which is why the same relation could
# not be reused for a subject of another gender. The lemma and its four forms
# live here instead; the identifiers are kept for corpus compatibility.
